items.title: USN-9066-1: Linux kernel (HWE) vulnerabilities
items.summary: It was discovered that some AMD processors did not properly perform Reverse Map Table (RMP) checks when the IOMMU accessed certain host buffers. A local attacker with hypervisor access could possibly use this to trigger an out-of-bounds condition and compromise the integrity of SEV-SNP guest memory.

items.summary: It was discovered that the GNU C Library incorrectly handled the ccs= option in the fopen function. An attacker could possibly use this issue to cause GNU C Library to crash or execute arbitrary code. items.title: USN-9063-1: Yodl vulnerability
items.summary: It was discovered that Yodl incorrectly handled certain input, leading to a buffer over-read. An attacker could possibly use this issue to cause Yodl to crash, resulting in a denial of service.

items.title: USN-9062-1: SNMPTT vulnerability
items.summary: It was discovered that SNMPTT did not properly sanitize trap data passed to commands run through the EXEC, PREEXEC, and unknown_trap_exec options. A remote attacker could possibly use this issue to execute arbitrary shell commands.

items.title: USN-9060-1: kramdown vulnerability
items.summary: It was discovered that kramdown processed the template option in documents by default. An attacker could possibly use this issue to read arbitrary files or execute arbitrary code.

items.title: USN-9059-1: ruby-jwt vulnerability
items.summary: It was discovered that ruby-jwt incorrectly verified HMAC signatures when the verification key was empty or missing. A remote attacker could possibly use this issue to forge tokens and bypass authentication.
